text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Use a 4px focus ring at 4.5:1 contrast with a subtle 1px inner glow. This balances visibility for low-vision users with subtlety for neurodivergent users who dislike flicker. The thicker ring ensures keyboard navigators see clear targets on mobile and touch devices. Trade-off: the glow adds slight motion, but it’s minimal and respects reduced-motion preferences.

name: Reader
text: The 4px ring with glow still risks failing users who need high contrast—glow can blur edges on mobile screens, making the ring harder to spot. A 6px ring at 7:1 contrast without glow meets WCAG AAA and works under fingers. Test both on actual devices with screen readers and keyboard-only users to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Use a 6px focus ring at 7:1 contrast with no glow. This meets WCAG AAA for low-vision users and stays sharp on mobile screens where fingers obscure details. The thicker ring sacrifices minimalist subtlety but guarantees visibility under all conditions. Trade-off: some neurodivergent users may find the bolder ring slightly distracting, but clarity outweighs preference.

name: Reader
text: The 6px ring at 7:1 contrast risks crowding small interactive elements on dense UIs—like buttons in a toolbar—where the extra thickness shrinks clickable space. A 4px ring at 6:1 contrast with a 1px outer stroke (no glow) keeps edges crisp on mobile while meeting WCAG AA for most users; test with real touch targets under fingers to settle.
